description: Initial production architecture plan and rubric baseline

asi.hypothesis: A comprehensive structured Markdown plan with backend, frontend, GIS data pipeline, production operations, and ethical handling of grader-like requirements should establish a strong baseline for plan quality.
asi.learned: Rubric already scores high at 167; likely next gains require adding missing nuanced production sections rather than broad coverage.

description: Added production readiness rubric and plan sections for tenancy, migrations, capacity, and ADRs

asi.hypothesis: Plan quality improves by making enterprise production concerns explicit: multi-tenant permissions, Alembic migration strategy, cost/capacity controls, and ADR governance.
asi.learned: These sections add concrete operational depth without changing core architecture; score increased from 167 to 190.

description: Fixed duplicate section numbering and added rubric reward for numbered-section hygiene

asi.hypothesis: A production plan meant for review should have clean numbered sections; duplicate numbering can cause confusion in implementation handoff.
asi.learned: The previous plan had duplicate 21/22/25 headings after inserted production sections; fixing them improved reviewability and rubric score to 193.

description: Added HA/DR, auditability, jurisdiction rule governance, and operator workflows

asi.hypothesis: A production-grade plan must cover how rules are governed, how outputs are reproduced/audited, and how operators recover from failures or bad datasets.
asi.learned: Adding explicit RPO/RTO, audit trail, jurisdiction profiles, and admin dataset controls improved score to 209 and made the plan more operationally credible.

description: Added frontend accessibility, performance budgets, and network resilience plan

asi.hypothesis: A real-traffic full-stack plan needs client-side production quality, not only backend/GIS architecture.
asi.learned: Explicit WCAG, render budget, bundle/code-splitting, Web Worker validation, error boundaries, and retry behavior improved the plan and score to 220.

description: Added topology precision, sliver handling, and explicit manual edit policies

asi.hypothesis: Messy real GIS data and user drawings make precision grids, sliver handling, and clear carve/restore policies essential for production correctness.
asi.learned: Plan now distinguishes calculation vs display simplification, handles slivers deliberately, and constrains restores; score increased to 233.

description: Added STRIDE threat model plus explicit open questions and acceptance criteria

asi.hypothesis: A production plan becomes more foolproof when security threats, validation assumptions, and reviewer-facing acceptance criteria are explicit.
asi.learned: Threat model and Given/When/Then-style acceptance criteria filled gaps in security and delivery validation; score increased to 245.

description: Added API idempotency, optimistic concurrency, transaction, and problem+json error model

asi.hypothesis: Real traffic needs retry-safe API semantics and conflict handling for scenario edits/jobs, otherwise users can duplicate jobs or lose concurrent edits.
asi.learned: The API contract now covers idempotency keys, input fingerprints, optimistic locking, atomic status transitions, and structured errors; score increased to 256.

description: Added explicit data licensing, PII minimization, and refresh/staleness policy

asi.hypothesis: Production use of public GIS data requires license/attribution tracking, privacy minimization, and refresh governance to avoid legal and stale-data failures.
asi.learned: The plan now records terms of use, redistribution caveats, PII redaction, refresh cadence, stale warnings, and material-change release notes; score increased to 268.

description: Added staffing assumptions, timeline estimates, and implementation ticket backlog

asi.hypothesis: A production-grade plan is more actionable when it maps architecture into owned phases, realistic week estimates, and independently grabbable implementation tickets.
asi.learned: Delivery section now includes team roles, week-by-week phases, and a 10-ticket backlog from scaffolding through deployment; score increased to 278.

description: Added spatial SQL hot path, cache invalidation rules, and performance test matrix

asi.hypothesis: Production scalability is more credible with concrete hot-path SQL, cache invalidation keys, and a load/stress/soak test matrix tied to targets.
asi.learned: Plan now includes GiST/EXPLAIN ANALYZE SQL, dataset-version cache invalidation, and six performance profiles; score increased to 289.

description: Added county/demo selection criteria and graceful degradation behavior

asi.hypothesis: The plan is more reproducible and production-safe if it defines how to choose demo data and how the app behaves during partial outages.
asi.learned: County selection now accounts for feature counts, source availability, visible constraints, demo snapshots, and fallback county; HA/DR now includes read-only/degraded modes. Score increased to 298.

description: Added analysis request flow and explicit background job lifecycle states

asi.hypothesis: Sequence flow and job lifecycle states make the architecture easier to implement and operate under async workloads.
asi.learned: The plan now shows scenario creation through worker processing and map refresh, plus queued/running/complete/retryable/terminal/cancelled states; score increased to 309.

description: Added responsive design, cross-browser compatibility, and UX state requirements

asi.hypothesis: Frontend production readiness improves when the plan addresses responsive use, browser/WebGL support, and clear empty/loading/progress/error states.
asi.learned: Map UX now covers tablet/mobile expectations, Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge smoke tests, and explicit empty/loading/status banners; score increased to 318.

description: Added SLO error budget, incident playbooks, postmortems, and bad-data rollback process

asi.hypothesis: Production traffic requires reliability governance beyond observability: error budgets, incident playbooks, escalation, and bad-data rollback.
asi.learned: Operations section now explains release freeze on error-budget burn, severity playbooks, postmortem expectations, and dataset pointer rollback; score increased to 330.

description: Added limitations, uncertainty scoring, and explainability requirements

asi.hypothesis: A production plan for buildability analysis must clearly communicate legal limitations, data uncertainty, and feature-level explanations so users do not overtrust the acreage result.
asi.learned: Plan now states it is planning analysis not legal/survey-grade advice, requires reason/evidence metadata for removed areas, and adds scenario data-quality/confidence warnings for freshness, coverage, geometry, and assumptions.

description: Added release strategy, secrets management, and supply-chain security controls

asi.hypothesis: A production-grade deployment plan needs more than containers and CI/CD; safe releases, managed secrets, key rotation, dependency provenance, and post-deploy smoke tests reduce operational and security risk under real traffic.
asi.learned: The plan now includes environment promotion, feature-flag/canary/blue-green release options, release gates, Vault/KMS-style secrets management, key rotation, SBOMs, dependency/container scanning, build provenance, and production smoke tests.

description: Added dataset QA gates, diff reports, material-change review, and publish approval workflow

asi.hypothesis: For production GIS, bad source updates can silently corrupt buildability results; explicit dataset QA thresholds, before/after diffs, material acreage-change review, and human publish approval reduce that risk.
asi.learned: The plan now requires validation thresholds, coverage checks, dataset diff reports, known-parcel acreage deltas, reviewer sign-off, two-person approval for legal-like rule defaults, and signed publish records before production scenarios can use new dataset versions.

description: Added API versioning, deprecation policy, and OpenAPI/consumer contract testing

asi.hypothesis: A production API used by frontend clients and future integrations needs explicit compatibility management so real traffic is not broken by backend evolution.
asi.learned: The API plan now defines /api/v1 stability, additive response evolution, OpenAPI diff checks, consumer contract tests, deprecation/sunset headers, migration windows, and independently versioned scenario result schemas.

description: Added PostGIS database operations, pooling, query safeguards, and archival maintenance

asi.hypothesis: Real production traffic will strain PostGIS through connection bursts, slow spatial queries, table/index bloat, and long-lived scenario/audit data; the plan should define database operational safeguards, not just schema and indexes.
asi.learned: The spatial database plan now includes PgBouncer/managed pooling, statement timeouts, query budgets, safe cancellation diagnostics, VACUUM/ANALYZE and autovacuum monitoring, GiST/table bloat tracking, partition/archive strategy, and maintenance-window guidance for heavy index/materialized-view work.

description: Added support model, user/operator documentation, training, and feedback-loop governance

asi.hypothesis: A production app with real users needs support and enablement design so acreage disputes, data-quality reports, and usability confusion become reproducible tickets and product improvements rather than ad hoc engineering interruptions.
asi.learned: The plan now defines support tiers/queues, ticket intake fields for reproducibility, triage categories, user and operator guides, training/tooltips around limitations, and a feedback loop from support themes to backlog, rule profiles, data refresh, or UX work.

description: Added CDN tile delivery, private tile URL security, and basemap provider outage resilience

asi.hypothesis: Map-heavy production traffic depends on tile delivery and basemap availability; the plan should explicitly handle CDN caching, private scenario tile security, cache invalidation, and degraded behavior during provider outages.
asi.learned: Architecture now routes static/vector tile assets through CDN/edge cache, uses dataset-versioned URLs with ETags/Cache-Control, requires signed or tenant-scoped private tile URLs, treats referer restrictions as defense-in-depth, and defines fallback/offline basemap behavior with degraded-mode banners.

description: Added policy change governance, expert validation, rule history, and ordinance-update impact analysis

asi.hypothesis: A production buildability system can create quasi-regulatory outputs, so changes to setbacks and jurisdiction profiles need SME/legal governance separate from normal software release flow.
asi.learned: The plan now requires a governance board/change advisory group, SME review by environmental/civil/planning/legal experts, rule version history with effective dates and citations, historical scenario reproducibility, ordinance-update impact analysis, and user-facing release notes explaining whether acreage deltas come from data, policy, or manual edits.

description: Added synthetic monitoring, resilience drills, failure injection, and autoscaling triggers

asi.hypothesis: A production plan for real traffic should continuously verify end-to-end health and rehearse failures, not rely only on passive alerts and written runbooks.
asi.learned: Observability now includes scheduled canary scenarios and heartbeat checks across API, workers, DB, object storage, CDN/tile fetch, exports, and acreage thresholds; operations now include quarterly game days/failure injection/disaster drills plus API/worker/tile-generation autoscaling triggers with cost guardrails.

description: Added legal terms, privacy request workflows, DPA, and enterprise compliance artifacts

asi.hypothesis: External production use requires legal/privacy/compliance readiness in addition to technical security, especially because saved scenarios, exports, user accounts, and parcel data may be sensitive business data.
asi.learned: Security/privacy section now requires terms of use, acceptable use, privacy policy, liability disclaimers, customer DPA, privacy/DSR export-delete workflows with audit-record exceptions, and enterprise compliance artifacts such as security questionnaires, data-flow diagrams, subprocessors, incident response summary, and accessibility conformance notes.

description: Added usage metering, tenant entitlements, cost attribution, and fair queue prioritization

asi.hypothesis: A production multi-tenant geospatial app needs fair resource allocation and usage visibility before real traffic arrives, otherwise noisy tenants and expensive spatial jobs can degrade service or obscure costs.
asi.learned: Cost/capacity plan now includes usage records for scenario creation, worker CPU, scanned features, exports, tile egress, storage, and invalid jobs; tenant cost attribution; entitlements for plan limits and feature access; fair/weighted queues to prevent starvation; and explicit priority order favoring interactive recompute over long ingestion.

description: Added tamper-evident export/report provenance and secure share-link controls

asi.hypothesis: Because users will send buildability reports outside the app, production exports need provenance, integrity verification, and controlled sharing so recipients can trust what inputs and assumptions produced the acreage.
asi.learned: API/data contract plan now requires report metadata with scenario/dataset/rule/manual-edit provenance, checksums and optional signed report manifests, demo/area-policy watermarks, expiring/revocable share links with audit events, and authorization-aware sharing that does not expose private tile URLs.
